sources.target_stage: Delhi High Court decision in CM(M) 642/2010 reviewing the ARCT judgment under supervisory jurisdiction.
sources.target_court: Delhi High Court, Hon'ble Ms. Justice Indermeet Kaur.

IK-52547606:L74:span1.text: contention was that the tenant Mohan Lal has sublet these premises to Anand Parkash and others including 'Parkash Trading Corporation' through Ram Parkash

IK-52547606:L75:span2.text: this contention was denied; stand of the tenant was that the premises in question had been taken on rent by Mohan Lal only for his son Anand Parkash and this was with the consent of the landlord who was living in the same premises and who was fully aware of the fact that Anand Parkash is carrying on the business from the said premises; there was no subletting.

IK-52547606:L78:span3.text: AW-4 had proved the electricity connection in the name of Mohan Lal; rent receipt was also in favour of Mohan Lal.

IK-52547606:L79:span4.text: AW-5 had proved the telephone record to show that M/s Parkash Trading Corporation had a telephone installed in the disputed premises up to 21.05.1963 whereafter the firm was dissolved and the telephone was thereafter shifted from the said premises.

IK-52547606:L81:span5.text: Partnership deed of M/s Parkash Trading Corporation Ex. RW-5/X13 was proved substantiating the averment that Anand Parkash was a partner in the said firm; thereafter this firm was dissolved and another partnership deed was executed Ex.RW-5/X15.

IK-52547606:L82:span6.text: it was the deceased Mohan Lal who was the tenant in the premises but since Anand Parkash was carrying on business in these premises from the very beginning which was also admitted by the landlord, no inference of parting with possession/subletting/assignment by Mohan Lal in favour of Anand Parkash could be made

IK-52547606:L84:span7.text: he had parted with possession of the premises in favour of his son Anand Parkash who was carrying on business in the same premises; ground of subletting under cite10†Section 14 (1)(b) stood confirmed in favour of the landlord.

IK-52547606:L93:span8.text: The landlord Maheshwar Dayal had been examined as AW-7 wherein in his cross-examination he has admitted that Mohan Lal had taken the premises for the business of his son Anand Parkash; further that Anand Parkash right from the inception of the tenancy was using these premises.

IK-52547606:L82:context-v4.text: 8 The ARC on the basis of the oral and documentary evidence had returned a finding that it was the deceased Mohan Lal who was the tenant in the premises but since Anand Parkash was carrying on business in these premises from the very beginning which was also admitted by the landlord, no inference of parting with possession/subletting/assignment by Mohan Lal in favour of Anand Parkash could be made

IK-52547606:L84:context-v4.text: The ARCT had examined oral and documentary evidence and drew a conclusion that the tenant was Mohan Lal; he had parted with possession of the premises in favour of his son Anand Parkash who was carrying on business in the same premises; ground of subletting under cite10†Section 14 (1)(b) stood confirmed in favour of the landlord.

conditions.binding: Mohan Lal; Anand Parkash; premises; date of business commencement
conditions.explanation: The prior court finding establishes the relevant disposition (business use) occurred from the very beginning of the tenancy, satisfying the post-9-June-1952 temporal requirement.

conditions.binding: Mohan Lal; Anand Parkash; premises; tenancy incidents
conditions.explanation: Evidence shows the son was a family member carrying on the father's business with consent, lacking the landlord-tenant relationship and transfer of interest/rent required for subletting.

conditions.binding: Mohan Lal; Anand Parkash; premises; tenant rights divestment
conditions.explanation: The tenant retained all rights as the sole lessee; the son's use was merely concurrent family use, not a divestment of the tenant's rights.

conditions.binding: Mohan Lal; Anand Parkash; premises; possession vesting
conditions.explanation: The tenant retained legal possession and control; the son's presence does not constitute vesting of possession in another or divestment of the tenant's right.

conditions.binding: Mohan Lal; landlord; consent status
conditions.explanation: The tenant alleges consent was obtained, which the landlord admitted to in cross-examination, but the specific written consent document is not explicitly detailed as produced in the provided text snippets.

conditions.binding: Mohan Lal; Anand Parkash; premises; concurrent user qualification
conditions.explanation: The tenant retained legal possession and the son was a family member carrying on the business, fitting the 'concurrent user' exception where no parting with possession occurs.

conditions.binding: Mohan Lal; Anand Parkash; premises; scope of disposition
conditions.explanation: The disposition concerns the whole or part of the premises as the son was using the disputed premises, though the legal characterization of this use is contested.

opposition.record: Landlord contends subletting to Anand Parkash and Parkash Trading Corporation without consent.
opposition.response: The landlord's claim relies on the existence of a sub-tenant relationship or parting with possession, which the evidence of family use and retained legal possession refutes under the 'concurrent user' exception.

gaps: Whether the landlord's admission of consent was in the required 'written' form as per the statute.
Whether the son's use of the premises for business purposes constitutes a 'parting with possession' if the tenant's legal possession is not wholly ousted.
answers.reason: I predict denial because the evidence strongly supports the 'concurrent user' exception (tenant retains legal possession) and refutes the 'subletting' and 'assignment' routes (no transfer of interest/rights). The prediction relies on the prior court finding that the son was a family member carrying on the father's business, which negates the statutory requirements for subletting or parting with possession.
